issues.description: The delivery contract gives opposite instructions for an unknown edit outcome. AC-1.5 and AC-1.10 require keeping the late event pending and retrying the same edit, while locked decision 4 says unknown outcomes are never retried or replaced. The verification section further allows a replacement after an unspecified "edit failure", which could include the transient or unknown outcomes that AC-1.5 forbids from replacement. No implementation can satisfy all three rules.
issues.evidence: AC-1.5 line 41 and AC-1.10 line 61 require retrying unknown edits; locked decision 4 line 68 prohibits retries for unknown outcomes; Verification line 82 broadly requests replacement after an edit failure.
issues.fix_hint: In spec.md, reconcile AC-1.5, AC-1.10, locked decision 4, and Verification by eliciting one operator policy for unknown edit acknowledgements; then state separately which bounded Telegram result permits replacement and change line 82 to test that exact result rather than generic "edit failure".

issues.description: The ambiguous initial-send path does not define whether the original single-eye event becomes terminal. Trigger: Telegram delivers the first checkpoint but the acknowledgement is lost; the current contiguous cursor remains on that event and the next drain sends it again. The spec says no replacement should be sent and only defines suppression of the later eye, leaving a retry of the original send neither explicitly forbidden nor terminally acknowledged. This can produce the duplicate notification the feature exists to eliminate.
issues.evidence: AC-1.5 line 41 and AC-1.10 lines 59-61 specify suppression for the late event but not terminal cursor treatment for the original ambiguous send; core/vps/notify-telegram.mjs:drainTelegramOutbox advances the cursor only when trySend returns ack=true at lines 1278-1283.
issues.fix_hint: In spec.md AC-1.5 and AC-1.10, add the required terminal state transition for the original event after an unknown first-send result, including whether its cursor is durably advanced or blocked, and require the lost-ack test to run a second drain and assert that sendMessage is not called again.

issues.description: The persisted per-round ownership claim has no crash-recovery contract. Trigger: drain A acquires the claim and exits after persistence but before editing or releasing it; drain B and every later drain observe themselves as non-owners and perform neither edit nor replacement. The late event remains pending indefinitely and can jam later feed checkpoints, violating delayed completion and fail-open feed behavior.
issues.evidence: AC-1.10 line 61 requires one persisted ownership claim and forbids non-owner effects, but defines no release, fencing, expiry, or abandoned-owner recovery; core/vps/obs-outbox.mjs:updateMetaIfUnchanged is only a non-transactional read-compare-write and explicitly retains a residual filesystem race.
issues.fix_hint: In spec.md AC-1.10, elicit and record the operator-approved abandoned-owner policy, then require an atomic fenced claim with an explicit release/recovery transition and add a test that terminates the owner immediately after claim persistence before starting a second drain.

issues.description: Journey #uj-3 / #ac-1.5 assume the late second family still arrives as a groupable spec-adversary event for the same attack cycle. Live dual is fail-open on primary only (adversary-nudge drives accept from family-1; family-2 is optional). After adversary_fired the planner can write execution-plan.json while family-2 is still in flight. Today eventForEyeRole keys type off completion-time planExists: once a full plan exists, adversary-family-2 emits {type:'eye', role:'adversary'} (curated as 'Adversarial da tarefa'), not stamped spec-adversary. The criteria never pin that a dispatch-stamped attack-cycle identity must keep emission as spec-adversary for that cycle even after a plan appears. Without that pin, delayed dual coverage cannot update the original checkpoint and instead spawns a mislabeled second feed line — the exact defect #574 is meant to remove.
issues.evidence: core/opencode/plugin/lib/obs-emit.mjs:eventForEyeRole (planExists===false → spec-adversary, else eye); core/opencode/plugin/lib/adversary-nudge.mjs:decideAdversaryNudge (primary-only accept); core/vps/notify-telegram.mjs:EYE_CURATED_ROLES includes adversary
issues.fix_hint: spec.md:#ac-1.1/#ac-1.5: add criterion that any eye reserved/dispatched under a stamped spec-adversary attack-cycle MUST emit type spec-adversary with that cycle's family+round/cycle-id regardless of planExists at completion; verification must cover family-2 completing after execution-plan.json exists

issues.description: #ac-1.5/#ac-1.10 prioritize never duplicating under ambiguous Telegram outcomes (timeout, lost ack, failed ref persist, unknown edit) and allow replacement only on positively confirmed missing-message. They never pin drain cursor/ack semantics for the second-family event. Contiguous cursor today advances only on send ack; an implementer can treat 'edit attempted' or 'unknown edit' as enough to advance past the late event. Then dual coverage is permanently stuck at '1 olho': no retry (cursor past), no replacement (outcome not confirmed-missing). The delayed-update journey becomes an orphan presentation state with no recovery path the ACs require tests for.
issues.evidence: spec.md:#ac-1.5,#ac-1.10; core/vps/notify-telegram.mjs:drainTelegramOutbox cosmetic loop (newCursor = i+1 only on sendResult.ack; suppress path advances without send)
issues.fix_hint: spec.md:#ac-1.5/#ac-1.10: pin that cursor/ack for a same-cycle second-family (or edit/replace) event advances only after positive edit ack or the single permitted confirmed-missing replacement ack; unknown/failed edit/ref-persist leaves the event unacked for a later drain retry

issues.description: #ac-1.2 and locked decision 3 require an opaque cycle identity and 1-based attack-cycle round assigned before either eye is dispatched, shared by every family in that cycle, never inferred from completion order or outbox cardinality. Verification demands dispatch-time proof including family-2 finishing after the next cycle's primary. Stated scope is only 'OpenCode eye-event emission' and 'Telegram checkpoint rendering/draining'; out of scope is 'adversary dispatch topology'. Pre-dispatch stamping cannot live in tool.execute.after emission alone — it requires the before-dispatch reservation path (loop-guard/reserveReviewAttempt). As written, the locked round-isolation criterion and the scope boundary contradict: either scope must explicitly include dispatch-time cycle stamping on the existing reservation, or #ac-1.2 is undeliverable without violating scope.
issues.evidence: spec.md:#ac-1.2, Locked decisions §3, Scope and constraints, Verification bullet 1; core/opencode/plugin/lib/loop-decide.mjs:reserveReviewAttempt (dispatch-time inflight reservation with family, no attack-cycle field today)
issues.fix_hint: spec.md:Scope: expand in-scope to 'dispatch-time attack-cycle stamp on existing review reservation (loop-guard/reserveReviewAttempt) without changing who/when dual eyes are dispatched'; keep topology/merge/ceremony out of scope
